english.title: Possess goods - duty not paid etc with intent to evade
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) knowingly acquired possession of goods, namely **(..SPECIFY THE NATURE OF THE GOODS..), which

(A)_[had been unlawfully removed from a warehouse or a King's warehouse]_
(B)_[were chargeable with a duty which had not been paid]_

with intent to evade any prohibition or restriction for the time being in force with respect to the goods under or by virtue of any enactment
english.legislation: Contrary to section 170(1)(a) and (3) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.

investigatoraction.description: Criminal lifestyle offence under Schedule 2 to POCA - consider confiscation order

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) There are DIFFERENT PENALTIES for possession of specific goods for export/import for which a prohibition/restriction was, for the time being in force and those apply to:-
(a) Section 3 of the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971 (offence wordings H3656, H3657, H3658, H3659, H3660, H3661, H3662 and H3663),
(b) Sections 20 and 21 of the Forgery and Counterfeiting Act 1981 (offence wording H3665) and (c) Regulation 2 of the Seal Skins Regulations 1996 (offence wording H3667).
(ii) See section 171 for general provisions as to offences and penalties.
(iii) See section 49 for forfeiture provisions
(iv) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.

other.penalty:

INDICTMENT: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine.
